I’ve been doing lots of assessments and ‘getting to know each other’ activities over the past fortnight to try to build a clear picture of the interests, needs and strengths of the children I’m going to be working with this year. Here’s a selection of some of the ones I’ve been using. Of course, standardised testing, teacher observations, professional reports etc will also play an important part in giving us insights into where the children are at and goals we will work towards too. 

So far I’m really enjoying working with Second Class and getting to know everyone a bit better. 🤩

#specialeducationteacher #muinteoir #formativeassessment #teachingideas #teachingandlearning

Since moving into the Acting Deputy Principal role last September, I’ve found I need to keep a much closer eye on all the moving parts of my week or month, especially at busy times of the year like September!

We use a school Google Calendar which is brilliant for seeing the big picture and knowing what’s coming up across the school. But when it starts getting very busy, I find it helpful to have a much simpler version just for me and my specific workload.  I use one of these free calendar pads from @the.learningstore and, at the start of each month, I pull out the monthly page, colour-code my key dates, deadlines, CPD and days where I need to organise multiple SET covers in advance, and then hang it up near my desk so I can see my timeframes, focuses and workload balance really clearly. 

There are only 8 things on my September page at the moment, and honestly, that’s exactly why I like it. 😅 It gives me a quick, at-a-glance view of the things I *actually* really need to think about without having everything else on the calendar competing for my attention. 

The Google Calendar helps me see everything. This sheet helps me see what *I* need to focus on. And for my head, I’ve found that distinction really helpful! 😊

#schoolleadership #deputyprincipal #specialeducationteacher #irishprimaryteacher #teacherorganisation

As an SET, these Getting to Know Me templates from NCSE Relate are a really useful starting point for building a fuller picture of a child at the beginning of the school year.  There are versions for the child, their teacher, other adults working with them and parents/caregivers, asking about things like their interests, strengths, what they enjoy about school, what makes learning easier, what has worked well for them before and anything important that the adults supporting them should know. Definitely worth checking out the Relate document itself and some of the downloadable templates: https://www.ncse.ie/school-leaders/resources-for-school-leaders/relate/
